content:
Reddit announces two upcoming changes that some long-time users are likely to strongly dislike.

The company has already implemented one restriction on old Reddit, and is now announcing a second. Additionally, RSS support is coming to an end…

Old Reddit

Reddit overhauled its user interface back in 2018, prompting strong backlash from users who preferred the previous version. In response, the platform promised to keep what is now called "old Reddit" running as long as people continued to use it.

In August, the company made its first change to that policy by requiring users to be logged in to access old Reddit. Now it is announcing that the original interface will only be available to users who have accessed it within the past six months, and new users will be locked out.

Reddit says both measures are aimed at reducing AI scraping of the platform's content (though that doesn't seem to be a problem if those companies are willing to pay).

RSS Feeds Coming to an End

Killing off RSS feeds is being done for the same reason.

This change could hit subreddit moderators particularly hard, as they rely on RSS for moderation tasks. Reddit says it is aware of this and recommends moderators use Devvit apps, such as Discord Relay.

Users Aren't Happy

A quick look at the comments section makes it clear that many long-time users are very unhappy about these latest developments.

What do you think about these latest changes? Drop us a line in the comments.
